#109677. Tech Report: Ubisoft states Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Tech Report: Ubisoft states Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet remarked mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet remarked mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which debuted last year.

According to recent reports, ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its upcoming operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

According to recent reports, outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft claims the fresh structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active customers over the half.

That mentioned, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

It has been revealed that the news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

It has been revealed that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a newly introduced Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

"Lose Track of Time" is a reference to "Life Is Passing Me By", which is a well-known cheat code in GTA: Vice City that speeds up the in-game clock.

"Everyone agrees it's more fun this way": Toby Fox won't tell his team how Deltarune ends until they've built enough of it

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person.
  • Earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief enhancement on the game's next and sixth chapter.
  • It has been revealed that but in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an upgrade for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.

Earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief enhancement on the game's next and sixth chapter. That one's apparently now a "structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end," but that doesn't mean it's quite ready for release, as "some notable scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation." I'd expect a 2027 release for this chapter, which is going to be a shorter one too.

It has been revealed that but in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an upgrade for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end. "Well, we've only just started…," he explains of the progress. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.".

Industry observers note that I'm glad they all think it's fun, the wait for me personally certainly ain't. I do wonder if this speaks to a certain anxiety over how the game will shape up. Following the release of chapter five I was subjected to all manner of theories about what's to come by my partner gorging on YouTube videos from folks who mostly just seem quite excited about it all, even if a lot of them sound wrong. So I imagine there must be a little bit of weight to all of those varying expectations.

Sources indicate that fox did note in the newsletter that "unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" so perhaps I'm speaking a load of hogwash! That noted, I'm furious that a character called Apple Girlington didn't make it into chapter five, so you can expect to hear from my lawyers, Mr. Fox.

Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • Recent findings suggest that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • According to recent reports, "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

Recent findings suggest that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

According to recent reports, "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

It has been revealed that moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

According to recent reports, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Sources indicate that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm right now ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

Sources indicate that the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

According to recent reports, world of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

Sources indicate that modern Family may have ended, but Julie Bowen has never stopped being a "mom" to her on-screen kiddos. For instance, Bowen was present when TV daughter Sarah Hyland got married in 2022, and both were part of that epic cast reunion at her wedding. Of course, Bowen also has love for her other faux kids, Ariel Winter and Nolan Gould. In fact, Bowen gave them a shout out during a recent event, and she trolled them in a seriously mom-coded way that's hard not to love.

Bowen recently attended the 2026 Baby2Baby gala at the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, California, a non-profit she has been involved with for over 15 years. While there to raise money for children in poverty, Bowen was asked by Entertainment Tonight for her thoughts on Winter and Gould living together “almost like real-life brother and sister.” On that note, the Claire Dunphy actress didn't hold back her hilarious response:.

It has been revealed that screw them. Screw the two of you. They live so close to me, and I never see them. I run into them. I’m like, ‘What’s going on?!’.

This is sitcom-level irony, but this kind of fun tends to happen amongst the cast. For instance, Winter has playfully called out on-screen significant sis Hyland for having a mini reunion without sending an invite to her and Gould. However, Bowen's comments are particularly funny, because they speak to the jokey but somewhat maternal relationship she has with her young co-stars.

Industry observers note that I can't see Hyland losing her “best fake daughter” title anytime soon due to Winter not sending an invite to her and Gould's latest abode. However, in all seriousness, Bowen’s comment is all in good fun, and she went on to gush about Gould and Winter -- who played Luke and Alex Dunphy, respectively -- as well as their firm friendship:.

I love them so much. I love that they live together. I love that they’re best friends. Everybody's like, ‘Are they together?’ I'm like, ‘No.’... They are roommates and best friends. They’re the best. I love them so much.

According to recent reports, not only are they NOT together, but it turns out that the best friend of your best friend makes for a good boyfriend. Winter is at the moment dating Gould’s best friend, after being introduced to him by her TV bro. Given she keeps her private life mostly out of public eye, she hasn’t revealed many details about the relationship. I'd imagine her former co-stars are enhancement to date, though, as Bowen previously shared that their close bond is why the cast has remained on such friendly terms.

According to recent reports, given Bowen literally watched the younger cast members grow up, it’s understandable that she would have a motherly relationship with them… right down to the A+ mom jokes. As for possibly hanging out with them, Bowen also shared this quip:.

Hit me up, Ariel and Nolan. Come on. Mommy needs you.

It's a moment like this that makes me wish a Modern Family revival of sorts would happen at some point. The cast's chemistry was just too perfect, and they clearly continue to have that bond off camera. I'm not sure whether ABC would be interested in such a production, but I'll keep my fingers crossed that it happens.

Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being.".

Sources indicate that you kick things off by embodying Eike, a "young woman who has strange dreams and sightings of twisted creatures in the woodlands neighbouring the sleepy Swiss village she lives in." She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods. You need to thoroughly inspect them, using a book to determine what is going on with them and what they need exactly; it's akin to checking the passport rulebook in Papers Please, hence the comparison.

In a recent development, after figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides. You may use care and precision to navigate to the correct corrupted emotion you have identified from your investigation and purify it. You may also use your tools to cause harm. Whatever you choose, your actions will have consequences." Ominous! You can also initiative your runs ahead of time, heading down paths that may offer you some boons here and there, like the option to restore a bit of sanity (it's one of those Lovecraftian kind of horror games, as loathe as I am that we still have to reference that guy).

Recent findings suggest that also be wary of the fact that actions you take out in the woods can affect your home and community. It's a roguelite with consequences! Mwahahha! Looks pretty neat overall, and has some tasty pixel art attached to it too. No release date just yet, but I'd assume it'll arrive no earlier than next year. You can wishlist it right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Right now, the devs behind Path of Exile 2 have a right to be confident. They've created a legitimate rival to the Diablo series, through consistent updates and worthwhile changes, fostering a strong community in the process. During a recent presentation, one of the key devs behind the action-RPG spoke on why he believes their approach to livestreams is much better than the rest of the industry.

Jonathan Rogers, technical director at Path of Exile studio Grinding Gear Games, went into the subject while giving a talk at this year's DevGAMM. "I've seen some truly terrible livestreams for game announcements," he notes. "Blizzard, I'm looking at you.".

It has been revealed that at least he's laying his thoughts out plainly. His first point is a simple one: show the game immediately. "Get to the damn gameplay," he states emphatically. "Nobody cares about your life story, nobody cares about the game's history, nobody cares about how you celebrate your audience or anything like that.".

I would definitely be on his side for this much. Too often I find myself sitting through a preview event, waiting for when the actual insight into the game I'm waiting for highlights up. The rest is often just fluff.

Industry observers note that his second point is another critical one: Lead with your best stuff. "The problem I've seen in presentations is they want to have this Steve Jobs, 'One more thing' moment," Rogers explains. "Don't do that. Lead with the best that you've got, show me what that is. It's just going to get people excited. You want people hyped.".

Nintendo is the obvious culprit here, to the point we're all on tenterhooks at the end of every Nintendo Direct, waiting for one last reveal or announcement. There's room to use such things sparingly, but it's a cliché by now. Give us the goods up front!

It has been revealed that his remaining four points on this subject are: Sell the story of playing; This is a tutorial; Spoil the game; and it's OK to be long. The first refers to how the game feels to play, the second and third are self-explanatory, and the fourth I'd consider more of a spectrum.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

If we're here strictly for a first look reveal, brevity helps to start. Get to the meat of what you want us to see, then save the rest for a post-show stream. But if you know you have a fanbase ready to devour every fine detail, then rinse whatever you have to showcase.

Path of Exile 2 is about to go 1.0, and it has hundreds of thousands of players. This is a team that knows what they're talking about, especially when it comes to what they don't like about official Diablo and World of Warcraft streams.

Path of Exile 2 is "f***ing genius," Baldur's Gate 3 publishing lead indicates – early access has been so successful "it won't even matter if nobody buys anything" after 1.0's free-to-play shift.

He previously served as Senior Anime Writer at Dexerto and News Editor at The Digital Fix, on top of providing work for Variety, IGN, Den of Geek, PC Gamer, and many more. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 39 million unique users have played Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 as of November 22, making it the biggest launch in PlayStation history across three decades and five console generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment announced.

The sequel set a latest record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles.

Across PlayStation 5, players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay in Grand Theft Auto VI, and have spent an average of 17.4 hours exploring the game’s world during its opening days.

Grand Theft Auto VI‘s launch also marked the largest number of newly connected PlayStation 5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays. Since launch, it was the first played game on 70 percent of latest PlayStation 5 consoles.

It has been revealed that “We want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2,” Sony Interactive Entertainment content communications manager Tim Turi remarked. “With [Grand Theft Auto VI], we worked to bring the best experience on [PlayStation 5] and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami this past weekend.”.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI  launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19. On November 20, Rockstar Games declared that the game achieved $3.79 billion in day one retail sales following 32.5 million pre-sales. Although Rockstar Games did not share exact unit numbers, the revenue total suggests roughly 37.9 million to 47.3 million copies sold, based solely on pricing across its $79.99 and $99.99 editions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own indicates through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, promptly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed].

In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A BBC report indicates Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.
  • Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A BBC report indicates Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

Industry observers note that "Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police stated following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated.

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom firm BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals.

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room, using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone.

According to recent reports, A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence, but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges.

It has been revealed that that struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking tech giant Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

Sources indicate that so far, Rockstar has stated nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent firm Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exiting DC, it's unknown if the DCU will continue or if we can expect yet another reboot. However, with one chapter closing for the studio, the start of a new might mean some long-gestating projects could get a second chance. Amid the corporate change, people have been asking about Keanu Reeves' long-discussed Constantine sequel again, and honestly, I don’t hate the possibility of seeing the 2005 movie finally get a follow-up.

Industry observers note that A Constantine sequel has technically been "in the works" since 2022, and at the time, it was reported that writer Akiva Goldsman was working on the script. Director Francis Lawrence has been committed making another flick centered on Reeves' DC character, and he previously confirmed the leading man was "excited" about the idea. While there was a positive upgrade in 2025, news has been scarce since then. Yet, when the director spoke with Collider about Sunrise on the Reaping, he gave John Constantine fans some hope:.

Well, I’ll tell you this. Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs, so this is not like a schadenfreude kind of thing, but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for 20-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it, and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it. So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity.

In a recent development, this is sure to be music to some fans' ears amid the major corporate shift. Jeremy Latcham, a Marvel Studios alum who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy, is stepping into the role of DC Studios CEO. As a result, Gunn’s DC universe might be over, and Lawrence -- who's sympathetic to the exiting CEOs -- seems to be confident that this could open the door for a Constantine sequel.

Of course, Lawrence is also upfront about having no idea what the studio has planned. For all he knows, they could want a different John Constantine for a shared universe. With that in mind, he’s also perfectly fine if the studio want to do a fresh take and allows him to make a sequel to HIS version with Reeves. In Lawrence's mind, two iterations can co-exist.

Sources indicate that at this point, Francis Lawrence has made it clear that the project is further along than fans think, as they have a script ready to go. The only obstacle in his way is a thumbs up from the powers that be:.

But again, we’ve been trying to make this for 20-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine.'.

Sources indicate that 2005's Constantine has earned quite the cult following. Believe it or not, Reeves wasn’t fans' first pick for the role, and that's because of how much of a departure from the comics his take on John is. The character has lived on in the live-action space since then, with Matt Ryan taking on the trench coat in 2014 for a short-lived NBC show. Ryan continued to portray Constantine in The CW’s Arrowverse and voiced the DC antihero in various animated works through 2024.

In a recent development, however, a portion of fans still seem hopeful that Keanu Reeves will get another chance to play the character, and I’d love to see him back in the role. Considering Reeves' skills as an actor and his love for John, I have no doubt he can slide right back into the role. We'll have to play the waiting game on that front, though, as DC Studios has yet to reveal any upcoming plans that will follow James Gunn and Peter Safran's departures.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

Recent findings suggest that the star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

Sources indicate that on the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

Sources indicate that total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

Recent findings suggest that this is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

There's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in highlights or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

It has been revealed that alt Video is currently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

#109656. Quote of the Day from GTA 6 writer: "We want players to be emotionally in step with Jason and Lucia"

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (592 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamesradar ↗ Open Full Page

Quote of the Day from GTA 6 writer: "We want players to be emotionally in step with Jason and Lucia"

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has been in players' hands for a few days now, and one pretty major narrative has emerged - a dissatisfaction among some groups with the pacing and limited stakes of early missions.
  • "We want players to be emotionally in-step with Jason and Lucia, going through the highs and lows they do," he explains.
  • According to recent reports, those slower moments, Wiafe explains, are all part of "advancing at a rhythm that doesn't feel too off-beat with the player's own playstyle and choices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been in players' hands for a few days now, and one pretty major narrative has emerged - a dissatisfaction among some groups with the pacing and limited stakes of early missions. Particularly before Lucia leaves prison, the more domestic aspects of Jason's story has been a signficant talking point. But that slower pace was part of Rockstar's plan, as writer Michael Wiafe explained in a pre-release briefing on the game.

"We want players to be emotionally in-step with Jason and Lucia, going through the highs and lows they do," he explains. Rockstar wanted players to feel "the thrills and excitement that come with a rebellious rush to escape from economic desperation," but I think it also wanted them to feel Jason's anxiety about building a life for his family, and Lucia's restlessness throughout Chapter 1 that sees her so desperate to find meaningful work.

According to recent reports, those slower moments, Wiafe explains, are all part of "advancing at a rhythm that doesn't feel too off-beat with the player's own playstyle and choices. Distractions along the way, major or minor, are all welcome," and that means that when you do go off into the open-world to explore at your own pace, coming back to the story shouldn't require "a mental reset each time.".

Crucially, Rockstar doesn't want you to feel "an overwhelming sense of having to grind in order to progress the story." Wiafe points out that "there obviously is the option here to grind," but says that "the world is so rich and thought-out," that Rockstar hopes players can "just enjoy existing in it to the point where the experience just feels seamless from start to finish." The story, he says, "is happening to Jason and Lucia; however, players should feel they still have all the agency.".

It's that final sentence that's why I chose this as today's Quote of the Day, because I think it's where the disconnect lies. A certain subsection of players don't feel as though they've got that agency, because GTA 6 - far more than other games in the series - wants you to feel the investment in and stakes of its world. To some extent, the disconnect comes from holding on too much to what GTA has been in the past; i.e. a criminal sandbox where chaotic rampages are part of the soul of the game. GTA 6 isn't that game, and I'm not sure Rockstar is that studio anymore. But when some players just want to drive a sports car through a crowded beach, any mission - however optional - that asks them to paint a house or collect flowers for their girlfriend is going to be considered antithetical to what the series is supposed to be about.

Original Story: One of the coolest things about GTA 6 since release has been watching players discover all kinds of Easter Eggs, such as the Mario-inspired hats that were shared by our sister site Nintendo Life yesterday.

We reckon this is the best one so far though - a secret portal that takes you into a nightclub from the original 2002 version of Vice City for the PS2 (which technically means it takes you back to its 1986-inspired setting).

Recent findings suggest that the process of getting here is long-winded, and detailed in full in the video from Dan Allen Gaming up above. In a nutshell, you have to go to the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento and use the power switch and press a button to make the Malibu logo appear on the TV. From there, visit 12 LPL substations around the map without fast-travelling, and press the correct buttons in the specific order (from the video) when you reach them. You'll then get a text, at which point you head to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station between 7pm and 6am to find the portal.

It seems someone called Memelo was the first to discover this trick:.

Another really cool part of this Easter Egg is that when you combine all the substations together, the wording on the outside of them adds up to "Life is Passing Me By", which references a classic cheat code from the original Vice City. You actually have to use the buttons to enter this cheat code and make the portal appear.

As mentioned, you get two free items for your trouble as well, which are Tommy Vercetti's classic shirt and bike from the 2002 game. These appear as soon as you're thrown out of the portal and back into the so-called real world!

Industry observers note that finally, we'll also highlight that although pretty much all the footage we've seen of this Easter Egg has been exclusive to the Jason character, it does appear to work with Lucia as well. That stated, we've also come across many players who claim the portal isn't showing up for them, so we're not sure what's causing it to fail in those situations.

According to recent reports, anyway, crazy stuff right?! Who knows what other insane Easter Eggs might be discovered over the coming days and weeks - some people have mentioned they're seeing a "flashback" pop-up after completing the Vice City one, with a suggestion there may be another four flashback sequences yet to be found. Let's hope so!

In a recent development, have you tried this? Did you get Tommy Vercetti's items? Let us know down in the comments sectiobn below.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

Downing Street went on to address the concern of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

In a recent development, the leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else.".

According to recent reports, GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

It has been revealed that this state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Nioh 3 first launched for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam on February 6.

Here is an overview of the downloadable content and Complete Edition:.

In Bloody Insurrection, a Shogun Meets His End in Shimabara.

While pursuing the Spanish alchemists, Takechiyo learns that the source of Yui Shosetsu’s regrets lie in the Shimabara of the past. Guided by Shirogarasu, they transcend time once again, this time arriving in Shimabara in 1638. There, a battlefield where rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai join forces to wage a fierce and bloody struggle against the shogunate army. To uncover the source of the conspiracy, Takechiyo ventures deeper into the heart of Shimabara, encountering a host of upcoming figures along the way, including Amakusa Shiro, leader of the rebels; Tachibana Muneshige, a legendary warlord who survived the Warring States period; and a samurai who fights back against the alchemists.

Recent findings suggest that shimabara in 1638. Rebels have risen up against the tyranny of a local warlord and now clash against the shogunate forces sent to suppress them. Alchemists operating in the shadows and countless yokai join the fray, turning the conflict into a brutal, blood-soaked war. Takechiyo must navigate the various landscapes of Shimabara in the battle-fraught castle town, the vast underground caverns beneath Mount Unzen, and the rebel stronghold in Hara Castle.

Fierce Battles Against Storied Characters and New Yokai.

Takechiyo encounters Amakusa Shiro, the leader of the rebel forces, along with the legendary warrior Tachibana Muneshige, and the samurai who fights against the alchemists. Figures from Hell Rising make a comeback in this new story, and new yokai stand in Takechiyo’s way. There are also some familiar faces among the Guardian Spirits who lend Takechiyo their power.

Fresh Customization Elements and Endgame Content.

Upcoming Martial Arts are being added for each weapon type, along with numerous Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals. If players have both the first and second downloadable content and manage to complete Enlightened One’s Journey (the third playthrough), they will be able to unlock the new difficulty mode and fourth playthrough, Nioh‘s Journey, where players will find equipment drops of the highest rarity, Ethereal. This will take character customization and endgame challenges to the limit.

Newly introduced Content: The Battlefield of Carnage.

Sources indicate that A high-volume form of endgame content, the Battlefield of Carnage, awaits players in this downloadable content. Players will need to fight their way through battlefields teeming with enemies, defeat the boss of each floor, and press onward through a relentless series of battles.

In a recent development, each floor of the Battlefield of Carnage consists of a field divided into multiple war fronts. Defeat the boss controlling each war front to gain battlefield effects that provides an advantage on each floor.

Industry observers note that battlefield effects include steady stat boosts and other special effects. Depending on the player’s character customization, these special effects can create unexpected synergies and enable them to deliver overwhelming performances. Players are free to choose the order in which they conquer the war fronts and when to challenge the floor boss. The map provides information on the types of war front bosses and details about battlefield effects, so the player will need to devise a strategy best suited to their playstyle and character.

In addition, defeating formidable enemies on the battlefield will enable players to further strengthen equipment shrouded in traces of the Yokai Realm, which can only be obtained and generated in the Battlefield of Carnage.

Defeat the floor boss, purify the Yokai Realm, and seek out the most powerful equipment you can find. The ultimate challenge awaits, offering the hard-earned satisfaction that can only be found within Nioh.

New Guardian Spirits, skills, Martial Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, Graces, and more.

In a recent development, an edition that includes the base game, as well as downloadable content #1, “Hell Rising,” and downloadable content #2, “Bloody Insurrection,” which feature upcoming stories, enemies, yokai, bosses, and equipment. The Complete Edition also includes the in-game item bonus previously offered with the Digital Deluxe Edition, the set of 14 Infernal Weapons, along with the purchase bonuses Hellfire Equipment Set and Scampuss Furball Netsuke Charm.

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has noted it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

According to recent reports, since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

Recent findings suggest that fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose said.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole upcoming level.

According to recent reports, "It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

Blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who mentioned his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st.
  • In a recent development, original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have promptly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that an enhancement for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently declared the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

The Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

In a recent development, original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have promptly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

Given the fresh build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have mentioned anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ update's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

Recent findings suggest that one of the best things to emerge from Grand Theft Auto over the years has been the community's truly spectacular stunts: players soaring under bridges, leaping across buildings, and more. And with GTA 6's release this week, we've seen the first signs of the trend continuing in a brand-newly introduced world.

This TikTok video by user Gstitz from early in GTA 6, for instance, claims to be the "world's first" demonstration of a Mallard flying sideways between a narrow gap in a large building. It takes several attempts, but they eventually pull off the stunt without crashing or broken parts.

Another video from Hazardous is a more grounded (literally) look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and shows the YouTuber flinging motorbikes and cars around the map as they explore promising high-risk jumps. Some of these locations are tied to in-game challenges, so there are certainly breadcrumbs placed by Rockstar to encourage such ventures.

Granted, these are far from the truly absurd stunts we've seen in prior Grand Theft Auto games. But as a firing gun for the wider community, it's a great start. They're also among the most impressive things we've seen in GTA 6's opening week.

It has been revealed that it's doubtless been an eventful few days though. Players have been entranced by the slapstick violence and in-game social media. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has praised the game, despite not having time to actually play it. Eurogamer editor-in-chief Chris Tapsell also came away impressed, lauding it in his five star GTA 6 review.

Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap.
  • The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website.
  • Sources indicate that "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected owners was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one problem, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

Sources indicate that "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is key to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

In a recent development, "To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out.".

Sources indicate that unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by consumers on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the matter's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Industry observers note that given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender.".

Sources indicate that jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Recent findings suggest that jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

In a recent development, if you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

According to recent reports, after the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):.

Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

Note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

It has been revealed that there are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll enhancement this guide if the community finds more endings.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are right now being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

It has been revealed that looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

If you fancy some insight on something officially tied to Final Fantasy 7, Eurogamer's Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth review praised the game for its playful spin on the classic RPG. The third entry in the remake trilogy, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is coming in April 2027, and is looking good judging from early previews.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good folks over at Digital Foundry are still busy analysing all things to do with GTA 6's launch last week, and their latest comparison takes a look at all four console versions alongside each other - Series X, S, PS5 and PS5 Pro.

Industry observers note that they also go on to rank the versions in order, and perhaps surprisingly, Xbox Series X comes out on top versus the standard PS5. Two reasons are given for this, which are that the Xbox version supports 120Hz VRR to smooth out the dips in frame rate, and that the PS5 sometimes "suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X".

Industry observers note that "Although both target 30fps and maintain it during typical gameplay, heavy vehicle traversal and intense airport crowd sequences cause frame-rates to drop into the mid to upper 20s. PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.".

Visually, there are mentioned to be no real differences between the Xbox Series X and PS5 versions, although the Series X version does have "slightly more pronounced heat haze effects in one opening shot".

All of this is obviously beaten by the PS5 Pro though, which is said to "deliver the definitive console GTA 6 experience by leveraging its larger GPU, accelerated machine learning hardware and enhanced ray tracing features".

Industry observers note that "Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X - which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability. The Xbox Series S sits at the bottom due to visual trade-offs, unstable frame-rates and audio glitches.".

It's fair to say we never expected the Xbox Series X version to fare better than the PS5 version in this case, especially considering all the "plays best on PS5" marketing that surrounded GTA 6 prior to release.

Of course, Digital Foundry seeks out the most minute of details when it comes to technical analysis, and the differences between the Xbox Series X and standard PS5 versions aren't going to be major enough to suggest one version is far better than another. It's just interesting that they've ended up ranking the Series X higher in this instance.

Let us hear your thoughts in the comments, but please do keep it respectful! We enjoy the PS5 as well, and know plenty of people who are loving the game on that system. All the same, this is a fascinating analysis and a bonus for Xbox.
